findings.rule: Page helps a reader complete ONE observable job (task-contract-selected)
findings.evidence: The page bundles at least three reader jobs. Set up (H2s 'Create a Tunnels API key', 'Deploy the tunnel stack', 'Verify the connection', 'Add tunneled servers as connectors') is one job with one outcome: a tunneled server reachable from Claude. 'Rotate credentials' is a maintain job with its own trigger (schedule or suspected exposure). 'Remove a tunnel' is a decommission job with a different reader state and an irreversible outcome. The page description confirms it: it lists six verbs.
findings.fix: Keep this page as 'Set up an MCP tunnel' ending at the first successful tool call; move 'Rotate credentials' and 'Remove a tunnel' to their own task pages under connectors/mcp-tunnels and link them from Next steps.

findings.rule: Examples do not introduce a second object, alternate workflow, or unsupported capability

No example introduces a second object type or a capability the page does not otherwise support.

findings.rule: Heuristic T6 findings confirmed (imperative verb / one action per step)
findings.evidence: 1 confirmed, 2 rejected. Confirmed: 'Create a Tunnels API key' step 2 'Open **Tunnels API** and create a key' has two primary actions. Rejected: step 1 (line 15) and 'Add tunneled servers as connectors' step 1 (line 135) begin with the location phrase 'In claude.ai,' before a single imperative ('go to'); the rule intends one action per step, and a leading location qualifier does not add an action. The heuristic also MISSED two real violations because it only reads <Step title> text: Helm 'Install' body reads 'Read the Tunnels API key into an environment variable ... then install into a dedicated namespace', and Docker 'Provision the tunnel' body reads 'Read the Tunnels API key into an environment variable, then run the setup component.'
findings.fix: Allow a leading location phrase in T6a; extend T6b to the first sentence of a <Step> body, not only its title.
